best_for: Researchers, journalists and analysts who need to lay out and measure networks with thousands to millions of nodes on their own computer.

points.title: Built for big graphs
points.text: The project says Gephi handles networks from ten to ten million nodes, with layouts such as ForceAtlas 2, Fruchterman-Reingold and OpenOrd.

points.title: Statistics come built in
points.text: Community detection, centrality and clustering run inside the app. A spreadsheet-style data view lets you edit, search and filter node and edge columns.

points.title: Exports ready for print
points.text: Finished graphs export to PNG, PDF and SVG at high resolution, which suits papers and articles.

points.title: Free, with a browser option
points.text: Gephi is free and open source, run as a non-profit. For quick work without installing, Gephi Lite runs in the browser.

points.title: Linux Flatpak lags behind
points.text: The Flatpak is verified on Flathub but was at 0.10.1 when Windows and macOS were at 0.11.4, and it is x64 only. The project's own Linux download is a .tar.gz for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Better keyboard access in 0.11.4
points.text: The 0.11.4 release improved keyboard and screen reader support and fixed a modularity calculation that could run forever.

points.title: Install choices on Windows
points.text: The Windows installer comes in per-user and machine-wide forms. The Windows listing keeps 10 versions; macOS has Intel and Apple silicon images, and macOS and Linux list only the current release.
